mechanism: Personalized neoantigen mRNA vaccine designed from patient tumor sequencing to encode immunogenic mutations and stimulate tumor-specific anti-tumor immunity.
development_status: Exploratory Phase 1 adjuvant PDAC study. ClinicalTrials.gov remains not yet recruiting with an estimated July 2025 start, while Akeso announced first patient dosing in November 2025 for AK154 as monotherapy or with cadonilimab or ivonescimab after pancreatic cancer resection.
clinical_summary: NCT06913218 evaluates AK154 monotherapy or AK154 combined with cadonilimab (PD-1/CTLA-4) or ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF), followed by sequential mFOLFIRINOX, as postoperative adjuvant therapy in surgically resected PDAC. The assigned study is exploratory, open-label, single-center, and planned for 60 patients, with DLT and adverse-event incidence as primary endpoints and 2-year RFS and OS as secondary endpoints. Differentiation is supported by a personalized mRNA neoantigen approach in a high-recurrence, immunologically cold tumor setting, but no AK154 human efficacy results are available.
safety_summary: Human AK154 safety data are not yet reported. The trial's primary endpoints are DLT rate and adverse-event incidence, and Akeso reports only preclinical favorable safety. Relevant personalized/autologous immunotherapy analogs support monitoring for administration reactions, fever, fatigue, immune-mediated toxicity when combined with checkpoint therapy, sequencing/manufacturing constraints, and chemotherapy-related toxicity from mFOLFIRINOX.
management_tools: Medical benefit prior authorization tied to FDA label or NCCN compendium status at launch
Diagnosis, stage, surgical resection, adjuvant-line, ECOG, and prior-therapy criteria
Tumor tissue sequencing, neoantigen selection, and successful manufacturing documentation
Dose and course limits aligned to the approved vaccine schedule and combination regimen
Oncology pathway placement versus adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX and any checkpoint-containing alternatives
Site-of-care and specialty distribution controls for personalized manufacturing and administration logistics
Continuation criteria requiring no recurrence/progression and no unacceptable toxicity
evidence_gaps: No AK154 human efficacy, immunogenicity, or safety results were identified.
ClinicalTrials.gov status is not yet recruiting despite Akeso's November 2025 first-patient-dosed announcement.
No U.S. trial, FDA-regulated study flag, registrational pathway, filing plan, or launch timing was identified.
No direct AK154 price is available; treatment-year cost uses personalized/autologous oncology analogs.
The final dosing schedule, number of vaccine administrations, manufacturing turnaround, and combination positioning are not yet established.
ClinicalTrials.gov intervention text contains a typographical description of AK154 as a 'neotigeon personalized mRNA vaccine'.

sources.title: Akeso Announces First Patient Dosed in Phase I Trial of Personalized mRNA Vaccine AK154 as Monotherapy or in Combination with Cadonilimab or Ivonescimab for Adjuvant Treatment of Pancreatic Cancer
supports: Akeso announced first patient dosing in the Phase 1 AK154 pancreatic cancer adjuvant study
AK154 is Akeso's first mRNA-based therapeutic candidate to enter clinical development
AK154 is a personalized neoantigen vaccine developed using Akeso's mRNA platform
Vaccine design uses tumor sequencing and identification of high-affinity immunogenic mutations
Akeso states the approach aims to overcome the cold-tumor phenotype in pancreatic cancer

sources.title: RNA neoantigen vaccines prime long-lived CD8+ T cells in pancreatic cancer
supports: Analog individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccine was studied with atezolizumab and mFOLFIRINOX in resected PDAC
At 3.2-year median follow-up, vaccine-induced T-cell responders had median RFS not reached versus 13.4 months in non-responders
Prior phase 1 cohort included 16 vaccinated safety-evaluable patients and 8 of 16 biomarker-evaluable patients with high-magnitude neoantigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses
Supports clinical rationale but is not direct AK154 evidence

sources.title: DailyMed - PROVENGE (sipuleucel-T) Prescribing Information
supports: Provenge is an autologous cellular immunotherapy
Recommended course is 3 complete doses at approximately 2-week intervals
Each dose requires leukapheresis approximately 3 days before infusion

Safety warnings include acute infusion reactions, thromboembolic events, vascular disorders, infectious-disease handling precautions, and interaction concerns with chemotherapy or immunosuppressive therapy
Common adverse reactions include chills, fatigue, fever, back pain, nausea, joint ache, and headache

expected_launch_window.method: Used assigned Phase 1 status, estimated February 2028 primary completion, estimated November 2028 study completion, China-only single-center location, and lack of identified registrational or U.S. development path.
expected_launch_window.explanation: Even if Phase 1 finishes on schedule, AK154 would still need dose/regimen definition, registrational evidence, filing, and review. A 2032+ window is a conservative pipeline-monitoring estimate, and the absence of a U.S. pathway makes timing uncertain.

annual_cost_range.method: Interpreted annual cost as first treatment-year/course cost for an adjuvant personalized vaccine. Low equals 3 Provenge infusions x April 2026 CMS ASP payment limit for Q2043 ($56,269.192). High equals reported Amtagvi one-time WAC for an individualized solid-tumor immunotherapy.
annual_cost_range.explanation: AK154 has no disclosed price. Provenge is the closest marketed therapeutic cancer vaccine/autologous immunotherapy analog, while Amtagvi provides a high-end personalized solid-tumor immunotherapy analog. Range excludes checkpoint antibody, chemotherapy, administration, sequencing, hospitalization, and supportive-care costs.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced personalized mRNA neoantigen mechanism, PDAC cold-tumor rationale, combination with dual checkpoint/angiogenesis bispecifics, and supportive PDAC mRNA vaccine analog data against lack of AK154 human readout.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: AK154 could be meaningfully differentiated if it can reliably manufacture individualized vaccines and generate durable neoantigen-specific T cells in resected PDAC. Direct evidence remains early, so the rating is not High.

budget_impact.method: Combined high treatment-year analog cost with a narrower resected/adjuvant PDAC population and likely strict oncology PA/pathway controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient spend could be high, especially if combined with checkpoint antibodies and chemotherapy, but the initial eligible population is narrower than metastatic first-line solid tumor categories and would likely be tightly managed.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed launch proximity, Phase 1 evidence maturity, China-only site, no direct efficacy/safety data, and no identified U.S. development path.
disruption_risk.explanation: AK154 has an interesting mechanism, but operational or formulary disruption is not near-term because the program is exploratory and pre-registrational.

recommended_action.method: Mapped action to low disruption risk, Phase 1 status, lack of price/label, and absence of mature AK154 results.
recommended_action.explanation: Track registry updates, AK154 safety/immunogenicity readouts, manufacturing feasibility, combination regimen selection, and any movement toward registrational or U.S. development.
